newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI share issue price to be set by valuer.
newsitem.headline: QNI share issue price to be set by valuer.

text.p: Nickel and cobalt producer QNI Ltd said on Wednesday the price of its 504.03 million new shares to be issued as part of a merger deal with Gencor Ltd would be determined as part of an independent valuation of QNI assets.

QNI Ltd announced earlier that it would merging with the nickel arm of Gencor, giving the South African mining house up to 56 percent of the enlarged QNI group after QNI issues the 504.03 million shares.

"The independent valuation by Grant Samuel is expected to be completed by early July ahead of an extraordinary general meeting of QNI shareholders," managing director, Wyn Davies told a news conference.
QNI shares closed at A$2.68 on Monday.
Davies said the joining of QNI with Gencor's nickel division was a "merger of assets" and had been the subject of formal discussions between the two companies for the past six months.
Davies denied Gencor came to the talks wanting a 56 percent stake.
"Yes, they could have made a takeover, but they chose not to do so," Davies said.
"It's bringing us (QNI) up to a critical mass stage much more quickly, and that's important," Davies said.
QNI said the group would have a market value of about A$2.3 billion after the merger, compared with a current market capitalisation of about A$1.1 billion.
